Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original OpenTTD normal-zoom Underground terrain sprite source atlas.
Create a transparent PNG sprite sheet of EXACTLY 12 separate isometric ground tiles in a perfectly regular 4-column by 3-row grid. No text, borders, grid lines, labels or background. Each cell is the same size. Center each tile in its cell, with identical 2:1 diamond outline and identical dimensions. Leave transparent gutters. Each tile is viewed from the same fixed TTD isometric camera, top-left lighting, crisp restrained pixel art that reads after reduction to a 64x31 ground diamond. Tiles must be thin ground surfaces, no tall blocks or floating slabs.
Columns left to right: 1 solid unexcavated rock, a pale cool-gray irregular fractured geological surface; 2 cut face, the same rock opened into a low dark cavity with a clearly broken bright rear rim, rim contained within the diamond; 3 excavation in progress, matching cut face with some small pale loose rubble and a short orange support stripe; 4 fully excavated open floor, dark flat blue-gray smooth compressed gravel with no central rock chunks and a thin recessed rim.
Rows top to bottom: three genuinely different but equally toned texture variants of the same four states. Preserve the same diamond geometry and viewpoint across all 12. Solid tile must be visibly brighter and denser than open floor, also in grayscale. Conservative steel blue-gray and slate colors, restrained warm brown fine mineral specks, small amber accents only in excavation. No rails, buildings, vehicles, people, vegetation, words, cast shadow outside the diamond, drop-shadow effect, bevel or perspective distortion. Actual transparent alpha around all tiles. Original game art, not a concept scene.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: OpenTTD Deep Underground terrain sprite source atlas.
Edit target: the attached Underground terrain atlas. Create its Deep Underground counterpart. Preserve EXACTLY the same 4-column by 3-row layout, 12 separate diamond silhouettes, camera, size, transparent gutters, and tile centers.
Change the geology/materials to dark volcanic basalt: solid tiles in charcoal and neutral graphite gray, broad angular fractured basalt plates; recessed cut/cavity floors very dark slate with visible stone texture and slightly lighter rear broken rims. Small restrained warm copper/ochre mineral seams may appear, never lava, glow, flames or luminous liquid. Excavating column keeps its small amber support stripe. The fourth column must remain visibly flat open floor, with fewer stones than the second/third. All 3 texture variants remain distinct. Maintain bright solid versus dark empty cavity distinction in grayscale.
Style: crisp original OpenTTD isometric pixel art, top-left lighting, readable when reduced to64x31. Keep all twelve diamond outlines and cell positions unchanged. No objects, text, labels, grid, background or shadow beyond the diamonds. Preserve real transparent alpha.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original OpenTTD specialist railway vehicle sprite source sheet.
Transparent PNG, a perfectly regular grid with EXACTLY 8 columns and 4 rows, one vehicle per cell, 32 separate vehicle poses total. No text, labels, borders, guides, scenery, rails or background. Identical cell dimensions and vehicle contact centers throughout. Leave wide transparent gutters. Crisp original late-1990s TTD pixel art with small controlled color ramps, top-left light, orthographic elevated isometric game camera. Designed to reduce to a64x48 pixel canvas; vehicle footprint stays within48x28 native pixels, no exaggerated length.
The same physical vehicle in all 32 cells. Columns are EXACT screen headings in clockwise order: N nose straight UP, NE nose diagonally UPPER RIGHT, E nose directly RIGHT, SE nose LOWER RIGHT, S nose DOWN, SW nose LOWER LEFT, W nose LEFT, NW nose UPPER LEFT. These are eight different rendered camera views with correct exposed surfaces, never spin a flat drawing. End-on N/S views are foreshortened and narrower than E/W side views.
Rows: row1 idle, row2 moving (same silhouette with readable tiny illuminated amber running lamp), row3 working (cutter teeth visibly engaged/changed, small metal fragments contained beside the cutter, no large particles), row4 blocked (machine unchanged, small red beacon on the rear equipment). No drawn text or status symbols. Consistent vehicle length, cylinder diameter, wheels, contact height, shading direction and design across cells. True transparent alpha, no drop shadows.
Subject: Standard rail-mounted tunnel boring machine. A low yellow-ochre industrial cylindrical cutting shield at the nose with a circular silver toothed cutter face, short ribbed rectangular yellow body behind it, dark steel underframe and two small railway wheel bogies; a narrow dark blue operator cab/control unit at the rear. Exposed short black hydraulic lines and restrained gray ventilation louvers. Clearly a cutter, not a conventional locomotive. The cutter nose is the direction marker. Original utilitarian1970s engineering; compact squat form, readable silver tooth ring, no gigantic construction site, no track, no trailing wagons or separate support vehicle.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: OpenTTD Standard TBM missing REAR directions sprite sheet.
Use the attached yellow and blue Standard TBM sprite sheet as the edit target. Preserve its compact physical yellow cutting cylinder, silver toothed front disc, blue rear control cabin, railway wheel underframe, materials, top-left light, and native pixel-art style. Generate ONLY its missing rear three directions in an exactly3-column by4-row transparent sprite sheet,12 vehicles total, identical cell sizes/centers and transparent gutters. No words, grid, scenery, tracks, labels or background.
CRITICAL REAR VIEW GEOMETRY: the viewer is BEHIND the machine, looking at the REAR BLUE CABIN. The silver cutting face is pointed AWAY and should be hidden by the yellow body, never visible on the bottom near side. 
Column1 N: machine nose points vertically UP on the image; nearest/bottom object is the BACK of the blue cabin, then yellow cylinder extends upward, cutting disc at far TOP edge points away and is hidden.
Column2 NE: nose points UPPER RIGHT; blue rear cabin is at LOWER LEFT closest to viewer; yellow cylinder extends upper right, only its cylindrical back/body is visible, no front cutting disc facing the viewer.
Column3 NW: nose points UPPER LEFT; blue rear cabin is at LOWER RIGHT closest to viewer; yellow cylinder extends upper left, disc hidden.
These are actual8-direction vehicle rear views, never front views relabeled or rotated. End-on N is narrow; NE/NW are foreshortened diagonals.
Rows1 idle,2 moving small amber rear running lamp,3 working small tooth position change at far rim (no particles behind vehicle),4 blocked tiny RED rear beacon. All rows use identical body geometry and anchor. Preserve true transparent alpha; no glow outside the vehicle, no large shadows.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: OpenTTD Deep-rated TBM missing REAR-direction source sheet.
Use attached dark red/orange and graphite Deep TBM sheet as the edit target, preserve its reinforced compact cylindrical cutter, twin gray bracing rails, dark sealed control cabin, gray radiator and black rail wheel chassis. Keep original pixel art style, restrained metal texture and top-left light. No text, rails, background or scenery.

Column2 NE: rear graphite radiator/cabin at LOWER LEFT, orange cylinder at UPPER RIGHT; toothed front points away and is hidden by orange cylinder.
Column3 NW: rear graphite radiator/cabin at LOWER RIGHT, orange cylinder at UPPER LEFT; disc points away and is hidden. Real elevated rear camera views with correct end-on foreshortening, not flat rotations.
Rows1 idle,2 moving (small amber running lamp),3 working (slightly changed visible far cutter rim, no debris behind the rear),4 blocked (small red rear beacon). Machine shape and centers unchanged between rows. No glow beyond the vehicle. Genuine alpha transparency.

Transparent PNG with exactly8 columns and5 rows, 40 isolated wagon sprites total. Perfect equal cells; generous transparent gutters; each vehicle anchored at exactly the same center in its cell. No text, labels, grid, background, ground diamond, tracks, people or terrain. One wagon per cell, no locomotives.
Style: crisp restrained pixel art for a1990s isometric transport game, lit from upper left. Low compact vehicle that reduces cleanly to a64x48 native canvas, actual wagon no more than48x28 native pixels. Two small black railway wheel bogies, two visible short couplers. Redraw eight real elevated camera views rather than flat image rotations.
Columns1..8: wagon long axis oriented N(vertical), NE(/), E(horizontal), SE(\), S(vertical), SW(/), W(horizontal), NW(\), with correct end-on foreshortening: columns1/5 are narrow end views,3/7 are broadside views, diagonals are shorter angled views. Sides with top-left illumination differ properly, symmetric wagon ends may match.
Rows1..5: EMPTY fully visible dark empty interior; PARTIAL contents only fill lower half of hopper with inside walls visible; FULL contents heap above lip; SERVICE empty with a small amber marker lamp on the near buffer; BLOCKED empty with a small red marker lamp on the near buffer. Markers stay on vehicle and do not produce background glow. Same wagon construction across all load/status views. True alpha transparency.

Warm brown fine-grained soil and occasional pale pebbles in loaded rows. Earth reads as a relatively smooth gently rounded brown heap, no gray jagged boulders.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: original OpenTTD sealed/commissioning/connected rail-portal source atlas.
Reference image: existing gray masonry railway portal, preserve its squat compact flat-roof concrete/masonry housing, dark railway mouth and small amber inside lamps. Do not retain magenta; output true transparent PNG.
Create exactly4 columns by3 rows,12 separate portal sprites, uniform grid, generous transparent gutters, common size/contact center. One1-tile compact housing per cell, TTD elevated orthographic isometric camera, top-left light, crisp pixel art readable reduced to64x64. No words, tracks outside the housing, people, labels, grid, terrain background or extraneous objects. Identical housing in all states.
Columns door direction NE,SE,SW,NW. NE opening on far upper-right side; SE opening on near lower-right side; SW opening on near lower-left side; NW opening on far upper-left side. Actually redraw the housing from all4 game approach views. Keep its roof, masonry sidewall and mouth size consistent.
Row1 SEALED: mouth is blocked by a visibly solid rough gray rock/steel barricade, ochre-black horizontal hazard strip across mouth and tiny red side lamp.
Row2 COMMISSIONING: same mouth contains small centered narrow dark TBM-work aperture surrounded by rough rock; amber work lamp and subtle yellow structural braces signal controlled work-only access, not a fully open freight tunnel.
Row3 CONNECTED: entirely open dark tunnel mouth, normal narrow rail bed visible inside, green side lamp; no barricade or machine. No glow beyond structure.
Return all12 housings on actual alpha transparency, no magenta, checkerboard or shadow backdrop.
